Thanks Julia — high level mapping below. I also attached a brief responsibility diagram and our SIG answer matrix (spreadsheet) with references to evidence items. Short summary first, then specific evidence pointers you can paste into the SIG cells.

High-level summary (plain language):
- Hosted (Redwood API): Redwood operates the full inference stack and runtime. We manage compute, storage of transient model artifacts, networking egress rules (per region), and logging retention by default. Customers control API access (API keys), prompt content, and can opt into KMS-backed secret storage for model keys when using enterprise plans. Evidence: SOC 2, hosted infra diagram, runtime ops runbook.

- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Dedicated GPU pools reserved to your org within Redwood managed infra. Redwood still operates the runtime and underlying hardware, but we isolate compute pools and provide tenant-level audit logging. Customers are responsible for tenant access controls, API key rotation, and any inbound network configuration for private peering. Evidence: dedicated tenant isolation doc, audit log samples, SLA excerpt.

- Private (VPC / on-prem): Customer provides network perimeter (VPC or on-prem). Redwood ships a private control plane or agent; customers retain primary control of networking, KMS/HSM, storage persistence, and physical access. Redwood provides deployment automation, monitoring agents, and optional support (managed ops). Evidence: deployment guide, HSM integration notes, test-of-deployment checklist.

Responsibility bullets by category (copyable into SIG):
- Networking:
  * Hosted: Redwood configures outbound routes and regional endpoints; customers do not manage host-level firewalling.
  * Dedicated: Redwood manages infra; we provide documentation for private peering. Customer must approve/configure VPC peering or VPN on their side.
  * Private: Customer owns VPC/subnet, routing, and firewall. Redwood provides IaC templates and can run the control plane in-customer network.

- Key Management:
  * Hosted: Redwood manages ephemeral keys by default; enterprise option integrates customer KMS (bring your own keys).
  * Dedicated: same options as Hosted; can be configured to use customer KMS for isolation.
  * Private: customer KMS/HSM required for customer-managed keying.

- Logs & Audit:
  * Hosted: Token-level usage logs retained per our retention policy; we can export logs to customer SIEM.
  * Dedicated: Tenant-level audit logs provided + exports.
  * Private: Logs are stored in-customer or per negotiated retention; we provide log-forwarding configs.

- Backups / Model artifacts:
  * Hosted: Redwood stores model variants and caches; persistence handled by Redwood.
  * Dedicated: same as Hosted but tenant-isolated caches.
  * Private: model artifacts persist in customer-controlled storage.

Evidence references (attachments / links included):
- SOC 2 Type II report: attached (SOC2_cert_2026.pdf).
- Responsibility diagram: attached (redwood_infra_responsibility_diagram_v2.pdf).
- Completed SIG answer matrix: attached spreadsheet (redwood_sig_answer_matrix_v1.xlsx) — each row links to the specific evidence file.
- Runbook snippets and audit log sample: link to Drive folder (see Drive link).

Items that need NeonHealth attestations / configuration decisions:
- If you choose Dedicated and want private peering, NeonHealth must confirm VPC CIDR ranges and approve firewall/VPN endpoints.
- If you require customer KMS for Hosted/Dedicated, confirm the KMS provider and access model (cross-account IAM roles).
- For Private deployments, NeonHealth must complete the deployment checklist and sign off on network access controls.

Next steps / ask:
1) I attached the SIG matrix; please tell me which items you want us to pre-fill vs. which require your attestation.
2) If you want Hosted answers to reference customer KMS, we’ll need a confirmation ticket with your KMS provider info.

I can jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the spreadsheet if that helps.

- Jonas
